svg.title: Intent to artifact: admission and observation
svg.desc: A proposed six-stage path. Accepted obligations enter planning and a typed job. The actual action requires current authority and qualified admission before an attempt. An observer distinguishes an effect, no effect within coverage, and an unknown outcome. Unknown outcomes hold blind retries. Artifacts, evaluation, and delivery follow their required observations. Feedback can reopen affected uses; evidence and release retain separate owners. Full text precedes the figure in the chapter.
svg.text: Intent to artifact
Proposed responsibilities; not a live service.
1. Accepted obligations
Objective, non-goals, means, criteria,
authority ceiling and recovery duties.
2. Plan and typed job
Check the proposed lowering against
those obligations. A plan is not a grant.
3. Qualified action admission
Current grant, bindings and precondition;
reserve single use where policy requires.
DENIED → hold this action before effect.
4. Attempt the bound action
Record operation identity and dispatch.
A reply alone does not establish an effect.
5. Observe the outcome
Effect, no effect within coverage, or unknown.
UNKNOWN → hold blind retry; assign an owner.
Recovery needs its own current authority.
6. Evaluate artifacts and delivery
Proceed only with required observations.
Criteria and residuals retain their owners.
Feedback can reopen an affected current use.
Evidence support and public release require
separate decisions by their authorized owners.
Argument support; no new outcome or release.
